Duration::le¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::le(const Duration& other) const;
Series Duration::operator<=(const Duration& other) const;  // le(other)

What It Does¶

Compares two Duration values elementwise, testing whether self is less than or equal to other by underlying elapsed-nanosecond magnitude, broadcasting under ordinary N-D rules, and returns a Series of booleans.

Parameters¶

other (const Duration&)

The duration to compare against. Broadcasts against self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series at the broadcasted shape, one comparison result per position.

Examples¶

Example 1. 1 hour is less than or equal to 90 minutes.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(one_hour.le(ninety_min));

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=true

1 hour <= 90 minutes is true (60 <= 90).

Notes¶

  • le(other) is lt(other) || eq(other) — true whenever either the strict-less-than or the equality comparison is true.

  • operator<= is documented sugar for le — nothing is computed differently between the two spellings.

See Also¶

  • lt: the strict counterpart.

  • ge: the opposite-direction non-strict comparison.

  • eq, ne: equality comparisons.
